manifest.platform: Linux x86_64; pinned Debian Python image; GIL CPython 3.13.15
manifest.release_scope: Original native foundation; full language conformance remains separate

scope.event: Example110 default INFORMATION, positional WARNING and keyword ERROR reach both original native client MSG_WRITE and durable event journal exactly once. UTF-8/newline payload at the 8192-character adapter limit is preserved.
scope.event_open: FUNCTION-EVENT and SECTION-4-10-083 remain open: the adapter accepts 1..8192 characters while the related Display text permits any string. Rejection of empty/oversize events is a declared adapter limitation, not qualification of unrestricted Event semantics. Desktop rendering is not tested.
scope.resend: Actual SAFE-mode CMD1 RELEASE/FAILED followed by a native OnFailure prompt. Every new attempt requires an explicit RESEND answer. Two failures then repair/success, or failure then CANCEL, have exact independent operation IDs and receipt counts.
scope.repair: Controller recovery uses an independently identified real original-schema SET_MODE command, whose five DSS receipts are distinguished from procedure command attempts. No language function, registry entry or driver result is replaced.
scope.uncertain_effects: Only definitive RELEASE/FAILED is resent. Unknown outcomes and stale authority are not treated as safe retries; existing CMD/native-driver regressions remain separate evidence.
scope.manual_interpretation: Page28 defines RESEND as resending a command; page116 explicitly restricts this legacy action to Send command injection. Page117 distinguishes operation failures from normal False results. This suite uses actual operation failures and does not infer whole-group RESUME semantics.
